text:
jordan (PM): kicking off a short thread to land the rollout pattern for routing-v2. Top asks: per-tenant control, regional staging, and automated graceful degradation. Keep messages tight — ops needs a clear kill path.

lee (eng): propose: three-phase release: 1) internal dogfood (10% internal tenants) 2) limited external pilot (5% in single region) 3) progressive tenant ramp (25% buckets). Each tenant assigned to a bucket deterministically.

jordan (PM): agree on deterministic buckets. For enterprise tenants we keep them out by default and expose an opt-in toggle. Support needs a per-tenant kill switch accessible from console + API.

ram (sre): runbook sketch:
- Canary windows: 20m warmup + 40m steady
- Auto-fail criteria: +0.4% absolute error OR p95 latency delta > 30% for 2 windows OR generation-quality drop >= 4 pts on smoke set
- On auto-fail: route tenant traffic to fallback pool, notify oncall, mark experiment as paused

lee (eng): flag model: key = routing.v2.active.<region>.<flag_version>. Metadata includes pct, max_rps, excluded_tiers, and runbook_url. Example rule snippet in comments inside PR. We'll implement sticky assignment: hash(tenant_id + flag_version) % 100.

tara (analytics): metrics to monitor: success_rate, p50/p95 latency, rerank-accuracy (on evaluators), and revenue-proxy for paying tenants. We'll run daily Bayesian checks and a fast-boot bootstrap during canaries. Also recommend a shadow-control path for heavy tenants for one day.

jordan (PM): shadow-control — elaborate?

tara (analytics): for large tenants, send requests to both baseline and candidate (no user-facing change) and compare outputs server-side. If significant divergence, auto-hold. This avoids impacting customers while getting signal.

ram (sre): fallback sequence should be explicit: candidate -> cached-response -> reduced-batching-degraded -> baseline. Cache TTL=30s default for degraded responses. Add observability hooks to count each fallback type.

lee (eng): on degraded-mode: simplify model path (smaller batch, lower kv prefetched) to reduce tail latency. We'll add a circuit that forces degraded-mode per-tenant when queueing > threshold.

jordan (PM): what about noisy neighbour protections?

ram (sre): enforce qos via flag metadata: max_rps per-tenant + global regional cap during canary. Token-bucket enforcement in gateway. If quota exceeded, route to degraded-mode rather than full fail.

lee (eng): flag JSON will include: exp_owner, flag_version, seed, retention_days. retention_days: 30 raw, 180 aggregated. We'll also emit an experiment_id to telemetry.

jordan (PM): launch gates to progress beyond pilot (minimal set):
- No auto-fails in pilot region for 48h
- No significant quality regression on nightly smoke run
- Kill-switch tested in staging with a live tenant flip
- Dashboards + pager alerts in place

tara (analytics): add a canary checklist for data readiness: sample sizes per metric, pre-specified priors for bayesian tests, and bootstrapped CI for quality signals.

lee (eng): deployment notes: schedule small, avoid traffic spikes. We'll build a middleware hook to annotate requests with experiment metadata so analytics can slice.

ram (sre): add automated rollback hook to orchestration: if threshold hit, flip flag to baseline and demote nodes from candidate pool. Hook must be idempotent.

ops-bot: scheduled: routing.v2 pilot -> eu-west (5%) at 2026-04-01T09:00Z. CI: green.

jordan (PM): owners + ETAs:
- lee: flag PR + middleware: Mon EOD
- ram: runbook + rollback automation: Tue lunchtime
- tara: dashboards + smoke runner: Tue morning
- infra: tagged pool & qos enforcement: Tue EOD

lee (eng): one more: provide a manual "single-tenant revert" API that support can call (authz scoped). We'll include it in the runbook.

jordan (PM): good. I'll draft the customer comms for enterprise teams and circulate. Sync next Wed to decide go/no-go.

ops-bot: note: please add runbook link and PR links to this thread when available.
